To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
unmet needs in older people with dementia are associated to caregivers’ age, burden, depression, stress and social support, but not to PWD’s characteristics.

the most common unmet needs in older people with dementia were daily living activities, company and memory, and that the best predictors of unmeta needs were caregivers’ social support, burden, young age, and high level of anxiety.

unmet needs in PWD are associated with caregivers’ age, burden, depression and anxiety, and that the most prevalent unmet needs were related to daily living activities, social and psychological needs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the most important needs of PWD in Chile, and with identifying factors associated with unmet needs.
the identification of needs of PWD and their caregivers, and the association of unmet needs with their characteristics and with caregivers’ burden, depression, social support and anxiety.
the identification of met and unmet needs in Chilean PWD and their predictors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most frequent unmet needs in PWD were “Daily living”, “Memory”, and “Company”.
unmet needs in PWD with dementia are related to caregivers’ social factors and their level of burden.
the needs of PWD are related to the needs of their informal caregivers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the needs of PWD are not only related to the PWD but also to the caregivers.

it is important to address psychological and social needs of PWD and that the fact that PWD unmet needs were mainly associated with caregivers’ factors highlights the importance of taking into consideration both the PWD and the caregivers as targets for institutional support.
the needs of older adults with dementia are not being met in Chile, but that the unmet needs are associated with the informal caregivers’ characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the needs of people with Alzheimer’s disease and other forms of dementia have not been assessed before in Chile.
unmet needs in PWDs are associated with the needs of their caregivers, and that both should be considered when planning interventions.
the needs of older PWD in Chile have to be addressed, and the needs that are not met are mostly psychological and social.
